overview: This Senate resolution supports the goals of "Deep Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism Awareness Month," observed in March. Deep vein thrombosis is a blood clot in a deep vein, most often in the leg; a pulmonary embolism happens when part of a clot breaks off and lodges in the lungs, which can be fatal. The resolution notes that these conditions affect up to 900,000 Americans each year and are often preventable, and lists risk factors such as surgery, immobility, cancer, pregnancy and older age. It recognizes the importance of raising awareness of these conditions. It does not create any program or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on April 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say greater awareness of the warning signs and risk factors can help prevent deaths from a common but often preventable condition.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or provide funding for prevention or research.
